subject: Layered prepay proposal & staircase GPU onboarding — Olive Labs
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara@olivelabs.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Holt <m.holt@olivelabs.ai>, Olive Labs Procurement <procurement@olivelabs.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Layered prepay for Dedicated capacity — initial ask

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Olive Labs is excited about Redwood's serving performance. Procurement asked me to start the prepay/commit conversation so we can align on budgeting for H2. High level ask: a multi-year prepay (3-year) with a staggered GPU onboarding (we want to avoid big up-front capital outlay in year 1). Our internal preference is something like: year 1: ~30% of peak GPUs, year 2: ~50%, year 3: 100%. We also need to understand how TPM throughput commitments map to those GPU tranches and what purchases trigger provisioned capacity.

Specific questions:
- Discount bands for annual prepay vs monthly billing at scale?
- Flexibility to accelerate tranche delivery if usage outpaces plan?
- Invoice cadence and PO requirements for year 1

Can you share a starter proposal and any template SOW/PO language you need? If you can put a simple matrix (GPU tranche vs discount vs TPM baseline) that would be super helpful.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Olive Labs

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara@olivelabs.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Layered prepay for Dedicated capacity — initial ask

Sara — really appreciate the clear framing. Attached is a starter model (prepay_model_v1.xlsx) that maps GPU tranche, nominal TPM baseline, and the blended discount we can offer for annual prepay. Summary of our initial position: 

- Proposed staircase (flexible): Year 1 commit = 25% of target pool (lower CAPEX burden), Year 2 = +35% (60% total), Year 3 = remaining (100% total).
- Discounting: 3-year annual prepay => blended discount range 18–22% depending on final aggregate committed GPU-hours and TPM corridor. For strictly annual prepay (each year invoiced upfront) we can start at 18% and ladder to 22% if you commit to a 3rd-year auto-renew clause.
- Acceleration: we can include an "accelerated fulfillment" clause permitting you to pull forward additional capacity against credit (prepaid drawdown) with a 30-day notice; we treat acceleration as a conversion event and apply a pro-rated credit.
- SLAs/Onboarding: propose a Q3 canary (small pool) to validate latency/throughput; full tranche provisioning follows a 30–45 day provisioning window per tranche after invoice clears.

Open items we need from your side: expected TPM for year-1 tranche (baseline requests/sec and p95 latency SLO), PO/Invoice contact, and whether tax-exempt status applies.

If that sounds in the ballpark I can draft a redlineable SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signatures. CC'ing Lauren and Ben for pricing/contract sign-off.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Layered prepay for Dedicated capacity — internal notes

Nikhil — forwarding a couple of quick internal points for your reply to Olive: 

On Wed, 17 Feb 2027 at 08:20 AM Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sara — really appreciate the clear framing. Attached is a starter model...
>
My thoughts: we have room to move but keep the blended approach — offer a 2% concession off the top of your 18% for sign by end of Feb (so 20% ) in exchange for an explicit acceleration credit language and a committed canary for Q3. Also add a ramp SLA: if Olive requests acceleration and we miss provisioning ELT window twice in a year they get a credit equal to 2% of that tranche's invoice. Finally, make sure the SOW calls out TPM measurement method (30-day rolling median) and overage handling.

Action: Nikhil, update the SOW with the ramp SLA and the acceleration conversion mechanics, and include a simple invoice schedule (Y1 upfront / Y2 upfront / Y3 upfront) so procurement can map to budgeting. Ben—please review pricing tiers and confirm we can front-load the 2% promotion for close-by-Feb.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Sara Liu <sara@olivelabs.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Holt <m.holt@olivelabs.ai>, Olive Labs Procurement <procurement@olivelabs.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Layered prepay for Dedicated capacity — olive labs confirmation

Nikhil / Lauren / Ben — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed the staircase and the acceleration language internally. Olive Labs is willing to proceed on the following basis: 

- Agreed staircase: Year 1 = 25% GPU tranche, Year 2 = +35% (60%), Year 3 = remaining to 100%.
- Discount: accept the 20% blended discount (as Lauren proposed) if we sign the SOW by EOD 2027-02-26.
- Acceleration: we accept the conversion mechanics; Olive will give 30-day notice and Redwood will have a 45-day provisioning target per tranche.
- Ramp SLA: we want the proposed credit language for missed provisioning (2% of tranche invoice) included in the SOW.
- Invoicing: Olive prefers Y1 invoice on signature (PO to follow), Y2/Y3 invoices annually on the anniversary date.

I attached the PO stub (Olive_PO_#7842.pdf) for procurement to process once you send the DocuSign. Please send a draft SOW and the DocuSign envelope and we'll aim to return signed copies within your timeline.

Next steps we need from Redwood: 1) Draft SOW with ramp SLA and acceleration conversion language; 2) DocuSign link for signature; 3) A kickoff workshop date (we prefer week of Mar 15).

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to getting this into procurement.

Best,
Sara Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Olive Labs

[Attachment: Olive_PO_#7842.pdf]
